3V3.//can_supply: P52: the figures a rail's load is summed against. The module powers its own ESP32 from this regulator before anything on the header gets any, so its own draw is a load on the rail it supplies.

VCC.//feeds: P52: what reaches 3V3 comes in here, through a step-down converter, so this pad draws at most what 3V3 carries - an upper bound, the only one a record can give.
VCC.//: The 5 V input. DFRobot: '5 V DC for powering the board (cannot charge Li-ion battery)' - see power.feeding_vcc_charges_the_battery, verified. It is a pad that works both ways and only one of them is this board's business: with nothing on the rail it carries the USB 5 V OUT, which is why `direction: in` does not mean 'always wire it'. It reaches VSYS through a P-FET, not a short (power.vcc_is_not_tied_to_vsys), so the FET is the practical current ceiling and DFRobot rate neither.

strapping.note: D9 is GPIO0, the BOOT pin - held low at reset it enters the bootloader, so nothing may drive it low during power-up. D2 is GPIO3, the JTAG source select strap. Both are usable as ordinary I/O once running; neither is safe for something that idles low.

adc2_unusable_with_wifi.note: on ADC2, which shares hardware with the radio. A5 (GPIO11) is the one that matters here: it is labelled analogue but cannot be read with WiFi active. Use A0-A4 or D5/D7 for analogue instead.

onboard_led.note: the on-board user LED, silkscreened D13. Usable, but it will blink whatever you put on it.

onboard_button.note: the on-board user button, silkscreened D14. Already has a button on it, and cannot wake the chip from deep sleep.

not_wake_capable.note: outside the RTC domain, so these cannot wake the chip however they are configured. Everything else on the header can.

console_uart.note: U0TXD and U0RXD — the ROM bootloader prints here on every reset and the serial console uses both. TX is driven push-pull at boot, so anything that acts on a level (a motor driver input, an enable line) twitches every time the board resets. Usable in a pinch, never a first choice, and taking them costs you the console you need during bring-up.

spi.note: MOSI, MISO, SCK and SS: the hardware SPI bus, silkscreened MO, MI, SCK and A4. A design with no SPI may use them — but they are taken LAST, because the assigner spent the whole bus on two LEDs and a button when nothing marked it, and a later SPI part then had nowhere to go. Recorded 2026-09-29 (backlog P3).

i2c.note: SDA and SCL: the hardware I2C bus. Same reasoning as spi. The smart bin never hit this only because its rangefinder claims both pins before anything else is placed.

deep_sleep.//simulated_by_wokwi: Established by experiment on the C6 - Wokwi wakes from a timer but not from a GPIO. Assumed to hold for the S3 stand-in; not retested.
deep_sleep.//polarity_is_a_wiring_decision: Which level wakes the chip is NOT a fact about this board - it follows from how the buttons are wired, so it lives in config.WAKE_ON_HIGH. What IS a fact about this board is the line above: one level applies to every ext1 pin at once, so every wake source must agree.
deep_sleep.//micropython_low_level_wake_bug: MicroPython #17334 (a pin stuck asserted after a low-level wake) is open upstream, reported on a C6 with v1.25.0. It has NOT been observed on any board in this project - nothing here has run on hardware - and whether it affects the S3 is untested. It is a reason to prefer waking on HIGH, not a measured fault. (Corrected 2026-10-01, P63: this note said it 'was hit on the C6' and quoted one project's config value, which had since changed.)

hardware_revisions.source: DFRobot's wiki carries two Board Overview tabs, and the schematics zip carries both V1.0.0 and V1.3.0: https://dfimg.dfrobot.com/wiki/20529/DFR0975_firebeetle-esp32-s3-ai-acceleration-board_schematics_V1.3.zip
hardware_revisions.how_to_tell: Look at the chip between the BOOT button and the USB-C. A QFN marked AXP313A is V1.1 or earlier; a tiny SOT-563 next to two SOT-23-5 LDOs is V1.2 or later. The back silkscreen also carries the revision.

v1_1_and_earlier.3v3_regulator: AXP313A PMIC, DCDC1, 1.5 A (X-Powers datasheet, not DFRobot)
v1_1_and_earlier.i2c_pullups: 5.1k to 3V3 already present on SDA/SCL — they are the PMIC's own bus pull-ups, and the PMIC is another device on your I2C bus
v1_1_and_earlier.user_button: also drives the PMIC's PWRON through a diode, so a long press can power the board down and the pin reads ~0.7 V pressed, not 0 V

v1_2_and_later.3v3_regulator: TPS62A02 buck, 2 A (TI datasheet, not DFRobot)
v1_2_and_later.i2c_pullups: NONE anywhere on the board. Every I2C device must bring its own, or the bus does not work at all
v1_2_and_later.user_button: a plain button: 5.1k pull-up, 100 nF, switch to ground

wroom1-v1-1.title: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 & WROOM-1U Datasheet
wroom1-v1-1.//private_only: No public copy of v1.1 exists (searched 2026-10-04): Espressif's URL serves a later version, and the Wayback Machine holds v1.0 and v1.2, not v1.1. The facts that cite it were read from this privately kept copy; a stranger can re-check them only against a later version.

eta6003-datasheet.//url: The same document from LCSC: identical text, 11 pages, a different save of the file, so a fetch from this URL will not match the sha256. ETA's own site serves no copy (2026-10-04).

vcc_is_not_tied_to_vsys.note: VCC reaches VSYS through a SI2301 P-FET with a dual-PNP gate drive and a 6.2 V zener clamp. Functionally VCC follows VSYS, but it is a switch, not a short, and the FET is the practical current ceiling — DFRobot rate neither.

charge_current_a.source: DFRobot wiki 'Max Charging Current: 1A'; schematic V1.3.0 ETA6003 ISET1 = 1k
charge_current_a.note: Not settable in software or by a jumper — changing it means replacing R2. Battery temperature protection is disabled on this board: NTC is tied to ground.

feeding_vcc_charges_the_battery.source: DFRobot wiki: '5 V DC for powering the board (cannot charge Li-ion battery)'

regulator_3v3_a.source: hardware_revisions: the AXP313A's DCDC1 is 1.5 A (V1.1 and earlier), the TPS62A02 is 2 A (V1.2 and later) - the lower, because one record covers both. Both come from the chip makers' datasheets as cited there; neither was re-read at source for this field.
regulator_3v3_a.why_it_matters: What everything on 3V3 is summed against, the module's own radio included. DFRobot rate neither regulator.

module_peak_a.source: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 datasheet v1.1, Table 11 (page 15): 802.11b, 1 Mbps, @20.5 dBm TX, 355 mA peak at 3.3 V.
module_peak_a.note: The radio's transmit peak, which is the most the module itself takes. With WiFi off it is far less; the sum uses the peak because a brown-out happens at the peak.

deep_sleep_ua.source: DFRobot publish no quiescent or deep-sleep figure for either SKU. Espressif's ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 datasheet v1.1, Table 12 (page 15): Deep-sleep 8 uA with RTC peripherals on, 7 uA with them off. Its footnote 1 - add 140 uA for 8 MB octal PSRAM (3.3 V) - is attached to the Light-sleep row, NOT to Deep-sleep; v1.8's Table 6-7 attaches it the same way
deep_sleep_ua.why_it_matters: Would decide which SKU to buy, and is unmeasured. This used to say the N16R8's PSRAM costs ~140 uA in deep sleep; the datasheet it cited attaches that figure to light sleep (corrected 2026-10-01, P63). Whether octal PSRAM draws anything in deep sleep is a bench measurement, and until it exists neither SKU is preferred on current.

io_volts.source: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 datasheet v1.1, Table 9 (page 14): VDD33 power supply voltage 3.0 min, 3.3 typ, 3.6 max V. Table 10: VOH is at least 0.8 x VDD measured into a high-impedance load, and a pin sources 40 mA (typ) at VOH >= 2.64 V with PAD_DRIVER = 3 - so at an indicator's few milliamps a pin sits close to 3.3 V, and a resistor computed from 3.3 V gives at most the current asked for.
io_volts.why_it_matters: the voltage a GPIO drives, from which a series resistor's value is computed (P78)
